Shape distances for real landmark arrays

Source: R/geometry3d.R
shape_distance.Rd

Pairwise distances in Kendall's shape space for configurations of \(k\) landmarks in \(m = 2\) or \(3\) dimensions, computed in C++.

Usage

shape_distance(
  X,
  distance = c("rho", "dF", "dP"),
  reflection = FALSE,
  Y = NULL
)

Arguments

X

Numeric array of dimension \(k \times m \times n\), with \(m\) equal to 2 or 3 and \(k \ge m + 1\).

distance

One of "rho" (Riemannian, default), "dF" (full Procrustes) or "dP" (partial Procrustes).

reflection

Logical. If FALSE (default) reflections are not removed, so a configuration and its mirror image are different shapes. If TRUE, shapes are compared up to reflection too.

Y

Optional second array of dimension \(k \times m \times n_y\). If given, the cross-distances between X and Y are returned instead.

Value

A numeric matrix: the symmetric \(n \times n\) matrix of distances between the configurations of X, or the \(n \times n_y\) matrix between those of X and Y.

Details

Each configuration is centered with the Helmert sub-matrix and scaled to unit norm, giving a \((k-1) \times m\) pre-shape \(z\). If \(s_1 \ge \dots \ge s_m\) are the singular values of \(z^\top w\), the cosine of the Riemannian distance is \(c = s_1 + \dots + s_{m-1} \pm s_m\), with the sign of \(s_m\) equal to the sign of \(\det(z^\top w)\) unless reflection = TRUE, in which case all signs are positive. Then $$\rho = \arccos c, \quad d_F = \sqrt{1 - c^2}, \quad d_P = \sqrt{2(1 - c)},$$ with \(c\) clamped to \([0, 1]\). For \(m = 2\) without reflection \(c\) equals \(|z^* w|\), so the result agrees with rho_matrix and dF_matrix. Two configurations that are exactly equal get distance 0.

References

Dryden, I. L. and Mardia, K. V. (2016). Statistical Shape Analysis, with Applications in R, 2nd ed. Wiley, sections 4.1 and 4.2.

See also

shape_mean, shape_kmeans

Examples

set.seed(1)
X <- array(rnorm(8 * 3 * 6), dim = c(8, 3, 6))
D <- shape_distance(X)
round(D[1:3, 1:3], 3)
#>       [,1]  [,2]  [,3]
#> [1,] 0.000 1.241 0.951
#> [2,] 1.241 0.000 1.141
#> [3,] 0.951 1.141 0.000
all.equal(shape_distance(X, "dF"), sin(D))
#> [1] TRUE

# A mirror image is a different shape unless reflections are allowed
Xm <- X; Xm[, 1, ] <- -Xm[, 1, ]
shape_distance(X[, , 1, drop = FALSE], Y = Xm[, , 1, drop = FALSE])
#>          [,1]
#> [1,] 0.909222
shape_distance(X[, , 1, drop = FALSE], Y = Xm[, , 1, drop = FALSE],
               reflection = TRUE)
#>      [,1]
#> [1,]    0
